summary.headline: CleanMax FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 28% to INR1,295 crore and PAT to INR86 crore; contracted capacity 5.7 GW with at least 1.5 GW addition guided for FY27.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue and EBITDA each grew about 28%, with EBITDA at INR1,295 crore against INR1,015 crore, and consolidated PAT rose to about INR86 crore from about INR19 crore. Operational capacity reached 3.1 GW after adding about 1,400 MW, and contracted capacity stood at 5.7 GW including 2.6 GW yet to be executed. Management guided to at least 1,500 MW of RE power sales additions in FY27 but gave no financial guidance. Key new risks raised were Rajasthan CTU curtailment (Bikaner 2 substation at about 30%) and the proposed deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) rules, which management has not yet quantified.

segments.name: RE Power Sales (C&I PPAs)
segments.commentary: Operational capacity 3.1 GW plus 2.6 GW contracted and under execution, total 5.7 GW; about 90% of EBITDA, with EBITDA margin 83.5% and gross margin around 92-93%. Average PPA tenor 23.17 years.

segments.name: RE Services (build-own-transfer style)
segments.commentary: Operational capacity 555 MW with another 215 MW under construction; EBITDA margin rose to 19.6% from 14.4%. Revenue growth about 28-30% across both segments.

guidance_outlook: Minimum 1,500 MW of RE Power Sales capacity addition in FY27; management said it is very confident of achieving this.
No financial guidance given; management reiterated reported EBITDA has historically been about 1.1x run-rate EBITDA, described as a past pattern rather than a forecast.
Storage/BESS response to DSM and curtailment to be announced in about three to four months.
Management expects EBITDA margin on RE Power Sales to reach nearly 86% in 3-4 years from about 83% today.
Grid forecast for end of Bikaner 2 backdown is September 2026, which management urged investors to treat conservatively.
Net debt to EBITDA target range of 5 to 5.5x; asset-level net debt to EBITDA cited at about 4.3x.
capex_capacity: Added about 1,400-1,471 MW of capacity in FY26 (RE Power Sales plus RE Services) versus less than 500 MW in FY25; operational capacity rose from about 1,700 MW to 3,100 MW in RE Power Sales.
Contracted pipeline of 2.6 GW yet to be executed at start of FY27; management said 100% of capacity expected in FY27 is already contracted.
A 530 MW CTU project at Koppal in Karnataka (450 MW wind, 80 MW solar) is being added in FY27; a 525 MW CTU project in Rajasthan is about 13% of run-rate EBITDA.
Approximately 1 GW of the FY27 additions expected in STU projects.
Solar commissioning planned to be light in July-September 2026 quarter; module deliveries for solar to resume from September or October 2026.
Under construction in Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and Uttarakhand, adding new states; currently dispatching power in more than seven states.
demand_pricing: Data and AI customers are 42% of contracted capacity (about 2,400 MW), up from 14% (about 260 MW) on 1 April 2024; named clients include Princeton Digital Group, Iron Mountain, STT Data, and global big tech (Apple, Meta, Google, Amazon per management).
Repeat business was 74% of new volumes contracted in FY26; 82% of volumes are with AA/AAA or MNC clients, 96% with A-rated and above; 588 customers.
Contracted tariff on 2.6 GW under execution averages about INR3.85/unit (about 70% solar, 30% wind, negligible storage).
About 1,600-1,700 MW of the 5.7 GW is contract-for-difference (VPPA/I-REC type) with firm price exposure; management said there is no merchant price exposure on these.
Average PPA tenor 23.17 FY26 (22.73 FY25, 21.54 FY24); average lock-in about 18 years; no client disputes across more than 1,100 contracts.

Management expects module-cost increases from ALMM to pass through to tariffs; customer savings fall from about 30-35% to about 22-25%, with demand still robust; buying accelerated ahead of the June 2026 transition.
Reported grid uptime 99.24% in FY26; wind PLF rose from 32% to 35%, while solar PLF was slightly lower on weaker radiation.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Iran war and supply constraints on capex, module costs and interest rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not seen material adverse movement in equipment availability or capital costs attributable to the Iran war, while acknowledging a volatile situation.

qa_highlights.question: Share of under-construction CTU capacity, curtailment exposure and PPA protection?
qa_highlights.answer: The 530 MW Koppal CTU project is mostly wind in South India where curtailment is seen as minimal; PPAs give no protection if the grid curtails, since corporate customers do not pay for performance.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the new deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) on revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: No final decision and no internal impact estimate yet; the rules are sub-judice and the government is in talks. Storage is being evaluated to limit DSM downside, with an update in three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Nature of INR414 crore pre-tax cash flow hedge gain and negative minority interest?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedge is a balance-sheet fair-value entry on VPPA/I-REC contracts with zero P&L impact given fixed tariffs; minority interest is negative because young SPVs (asset age under two years) carry interest and depreciation before profits.

qa_highlights.question: BESS in the contracted portfolio and tariffs?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 5-7 MW of BESS within the 2,600 MW under execution; management would not separate tariffs for storage.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of rising module prices on IRRs?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariffs are expected to adjust to module costs; management said it prices to a constant target IRR, with no expected impact on margins or volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin lower than utility peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Scale and higher SG&A from business development, multi-state offices and 13 MW average PPA size; margin expected to rise to about 86% in 3-4 years, with the 2-3 point gap offset by higher tariffs.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost outlook and Bikaner curtailment timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Refinancing may lower costs, but management would not make bold bets given macro risk. Bikaner 2 substation curtailment is about 30%; grid expects end by September 2026 but management urged more conservatism.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 pipeline mix and data-centre share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no reason for the wind/solar mix or the Data and AI share (42% at both start and end of FY26) to change, and says FY27 additions are already fully contracted.

qa_highlights.question: Is run-rate EBITDA adjusted for curtailment, and EBITDA per MW?
qa_highlights.answer: Run-rate EBITDA is not adjusted for curtailment and assumes about 1-1.5% grid downtime; management says per-MW EBITDA is 30-35% higher on a DC basis versus peers using AC.

risks_watch: Rajasthan CTU curtailment: Bikaner 2 at about 30%; management sized impact at about 2.5% of run-rate EBITDA for six months at 40% backdown and about 6.5% for a full year at 50%.
DSM rules: impact not yet quantified; rules are sub-judice, and forecasting improvements are needed industry-wide.
Module cost step-up from ALMM rules from June 2026 and possible timing slippage; solar contracting paused pending government decision.
Rising interest rate environment could offset refinancing benefits; 40% of debt is fixed rate.
Ramp-up of new assets: revenue stabilisation takes three to six months after COD, and the asset-level net debt build-up depends on this.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, contracting and customer quality, and forthright on the curtailment numbers. Cautious and non-committal on DSM impact, interest cost direction and the Apple JV terms, saying the figures are not yet mature or will not be disclosed.
key_quotes: We are very proud that over the last four years consistently, we have executed our plants and capacity within the budgets.
Run-rate EBITDA is not adjusted for curtailment.
We are not really taking a merchant price exposure is what I would like to highlight.
We have not yet seen any material adverse movements in terms of either availability of equipment or in terms of material movement in capital costs.
